bestFix.question: What is the best way to resolve the warning?

values.add-dep: Add the missing dependency (the rule's suggestion is right as it stands)
values.move-inside: Move the value or function into the hook's callback
values.memoise: Memoise the value or function the hook depends on (useMemo/useCallback), or move it out of the component
values.updater-function: Use a state updater function (setX(x => …)) so the state isn't read
values.use-effect-event: Move the non-reactive logic into useEffectEvent
values.ref: Read the latest value through a ref
values.remove-or-restructure: Remove the effect or restructure it (compute during render, handle in the event, key the component, use a store subscription, …)
values.leave: Leave it as it is (the warning is wrong, or the omission is deliberate and harmless); say why in notes
values.other: Something else; say what in notes

effectNeeded.question: For effects: is the effect needed at all? For memos and callbacks: n/a.

values.yes: It synchronises with something outside React (subscription, DOM, network, timer, imperative API)
values.no: It shouldn't exist; give the 'You Might Not Need an Effect' category in notNeededCategory

notNeededCategory.question: If the effect isn't needed, which 'You Might Not Need an Effect' case it is

values.derived-state: Updating state based on props or state; caching a calculation
values.reset-state: Resetting or adjusting state when a prop changes
values.event-specific: Logic that belongs in an event handler (including POST requests, notifications)
values.chain: A chain of computations across effects
values.notify-parent: Notifying or passing data to a parent
values.data-fetching: Fetching that a framework or library should do

realBug.question: Is the warning a real bug: can someone observe a stale value (or an effect that should have re-run and didn't, or ran when it shouldn't)?

values.yes: Yes: the omitted value can change while the hook doesn't re-run, and the stale result is visible (a wrong render, a missed update, a call with old arguments)
values.latent: It can't be seen today (the value never changes in practice, or the stale read is harmless), but it would go stale if the code around it changed
values.no: No: the omitted value is stable or irrelevant, or the dependency is unnecessary and listing it does no harm
values.unclear: Can't tell from the code and its visible uses

suggestedFix.question: Would the linters' suggested fix (add every missing dependency, remove the unnecessary ones, as the worksheet shows) be right?

values.right: Right: it fixes the staleness and runs the hook no more often than it should
values.harmless: Harmless: behaviour is the same (the added value is stable), the rule is just satisfied
values.reruns-more: Runs the hook more often than it should (every render, or on unrelated changes): a perf or behaviour problem, but not a loop
values.loop: Loops or re-subscribes on every render in a way that breaks the feature
values.changes-behaviour: Changes behaviour another way (a mount-only effect now repeats, a trigger dependency is removed, an event fires again)

whyOmitted.question: Why does the code look the way it does?

values.mount-only: Deliberately runs once (on mount) or only for some values
values.avoid-loop: Avoids a loop or extra runs the dependency would cause
values.event-like: The omitted value is read like an event's argument, not something to react to
values.stable-value: The value is stable, but the rule can't see it (a store, a form object, a ref-like value from a custom hook)
values.trigger: A dependency listed on purpose to re-run the effect, though the body doesn't read it

rater1.notes: The effect only needs to run when batchedData changes, and when it does it calls that render's updateData, so nothing goes stale. updateData is rebuilt by the action manager each render, so adding it runs the effect every render (a guarded no-op). The effect flushes batched picker changes to the parent's updateData, not derived state as the static reading says.

Biome only flags setAllCommands, a useState setter, which is stable, so dropping it changes nothing. The effect builds allCommands from stableDeps and stores it in state, which is a cached calculation; other effects then chain off allCommands.

fonts is app.fonts, an instance field that stays fixed while mounted, and getSceneFamilies() reads mutable scene state, so selectedFontFamily is a deliberate recompute trigger (see the comment). ESLint's and Biome's fixes drop selectedFontFamily, so the scene font list would never refresh; only Oxlint's [selectedFontFamily, fonts] is harmless.

Passing trails itself as the dependency list compares each trail instance, which is what the effect needs. App renders trails={[...]} as a new array literal every render, so ESLint's [trails] would stop() and start() every trail on every App render, and stop() clears the in-progress trail, which breaks laser/eraser trails.

rater2.notes: trails is an inline array literal in App.tsx, built on every App render, and its elements are stable trail instances. ESLint's [trails] would stop() (which clears the in-progress trail) and restart every trail on every App render, wiping laser/eraser trails mid-stroke.

rater1.notes: setFocusIndex (jotai setter) and lastSceneNonceRef (ref) are stable and harmless to drop. But elementsMap is a trigger that re-runs the search when the scene changes (the body checks the scene nonce). Biome's fix removes it, so search results would go stale after edits.

rater2.notes: elementsMap (scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap()) gets a new identity whenever the scene's elements are replaced, so it re-triggers the debounced search. Biome's removal drops that trigger; setFocusIndex and lastSceneNonceRef are stable and harmless to drop.

rater1.notes: editable is listed on purpose, as the comment explains: toggling it runs the cleanup, which commits the typed value, because React fires no blur on disabled inputs. Removing it, as Biome suggests, loses that commit.

sceneNonce is the trigger for in-place element mutations (scene.getNonDeletedElements() can keep the same array identity while elements are moved or resized). Dropping it would leave the scene dimensions stale. The effect drives a throttled (timer) recomputation, which is why it isn't plain derived state.

rater2.notes: sceneNonce changes on in-place element mutations, when scene.getNonDeletedElements() returns the same array, so it is the trigger that refreshes the throttled scene dimensions. Removing it leaves the stats stale while elements are moved or resized.

rater1.notes: messages is a deliberate trigger to scroll to the bottom when a message arrives. Biome's fix makes it mount-only, so the chat would stop auto-scrolling.

message is meant to restart the auto-close timer when the toast text changes, and duration is already covered by scheduleTimeout. The only caller (LayerUI) passes onClose inline, so scheduleTimeout changes on every render and the effect re-runs anyway. Biome's removal is harmless today but would let a new message close early if onClose were ever memoised. The static reading event-specific doesn't fit: this is a timer.
setSvg is a useState setter, so dropping it changes nothing. The effect does async SVG export and caching, which is imperative work rather than framework data fetching.

rater2.notes: setSvg is the useState setter declared in the same hook, so dropping it from the deps changes nothing. The effect does async SVG export with a cache.

rater1.notes: cb keeps the first render's updateState. Reducers passed to useOptimistic are usually pure, so it rarely shows, but one that closes over props would go stale. Callers usually pass updateState inline, so adding it makes cb unstable every render; a latest-value ref keeps it stable and fresh.

rater2.notes: updateState is the caller's reducer, usually an inline arrow. With [] the first one is frozen, which goes stale only if it closes over changing values. Adding it makes the returned dispatch a new function every render. A ref keeps the dispatch stable and the reducer fresh.

rater1.notes: Every caller passes cb as an inline arrow, and the composed ref callback only runs on attach, when the render's cb is current. Only late events (onLoad/onError captured at attach) could see old values. Adding cb gives a new ref callback every render, which detaches and reattaches the element (re-inserting head tags, re-adding listeners) on each render.

rater2.notes: cb is an inline arrow at all three call sites, so [cb, ref] would make the composed ref callback new on every render, detaching and reattaching listeners and re-running head insertion each time. Ref callbacks only run at attach, when the captured cb is current.

rater1.notes: This is Hono's implementation of useImperativeHandle, which forwards the caller's deps by contract. ESLint's [createHandle, ref] would ignore those deps, and createHandle is normally inline, so the handle would be rebuilt every render. It is a framework primitive, so notify-parent does not apply.

rater2.notes: This is hono's own useImperativeHandle, which forwards the caller's deps. ESLint's [createHandle, ref] would ignore them and rebuild the handle on every render, because createHandle is usually inline. whyOmitted: it runs only for the caller's chosen values.

rater1.notes: tree is a deliberate trigger: after each navigation the effect reads document.title and announces it. Biome's fix makes it mount-only, so route changes would no longer be announced to screen readers.

forceUpdate is a useState setter, so dropping it changes nothing. The effect subscribes to the module-level runtimeStyleChanged set and force-updates, which is a hand-rolled useSyncExternalStore; the static reading event-specific does not fit.

The explicit undefined deps argument deliberately runs the layout effect on every commit, as the comment says. No linter offers a fix. Deleting the undefined argument keeps the behaviour and makes the intent plain. No whyOmitted value fits a deliberate every-commit effect.

rater2.notes: Deps are deliberately undefined so the scroll handler runs on every commit (see the comment). No linter offers a fix, so nothing changes. whyOmitted uses mount-only as the closest 'deliberate run schedule' value; here the schedule is every commit.

rater1.notes: pathname is a deliberate trigger, per the comment ('Republish after navigation commits'). Biome's fix makes the effect mount-only, so HMR observers would stop receiving the current state after navigation.

rater2.notes: pathname is a deliberate trigger, per the comment about republishing after navigation commits. Biome's [] would report the runtime error state to HMR only once, on mount.

rater1.notes: elementRef.current is listed on purpose so that a swapped element gets re-observed on a later render (it is set by the setElement callback ref without a re-render). It is an unreliable trigger, but removing it means element changes are never re-observed. The proper fix is to keep the element in state via the callback ref.

rater2.notes: elementRef.current is written by the setElement callback ref. Listing it re-observes a swapped element one render later, which is unreliable if the node changes without this component re-rendering. Removing it means a swapped element is never observed. Better: keep the element in state from the callback ref and depend on that.

rater1.notes: dispatch comes from useReducer inside useErrorOverlayReducer, so it is stable, and adding it will not cause the reconnect the comment warns about. The effect connects to an external event queue.

isPending restarts the 2s reset timer when the user copies again while 'success' is showing: copyState.state stays 'success', so only isPending changes. Removing it lets the first timer reset the label in the middle of a repeat copy. The change is minor.

The resize listener only uses applyConstrainedDimensions. value.resizeRef is the same ref it already depends on, and initialSize is now handled by the separate useEffectEvent. Dropping the extras only avoids needless re-subscribes; they look left over from a refactor.

rater2.notes: The window resize listener reads neither value.initialSize nor value.resizeRef: initialSize moved into the fireInitialConstrainDimensions effect event, and resizeRef is already behind applyConstrainedDimensions. Dropping them only skips pointless re-subscriptions.

rater1.notes: Using Object.values(context) as the deps memoises the context object on its prop values, which is correct. context is a fresh rest object every render, so ESLint's [context] would rebuild the value every render and re-render every consumer.

rater2.notes: context is a rest object rebuilt on every render, so ESLint's [context] would recompute the memo every render and re-render every consumer. Object.values(context) memoises on the individual prop values on purpose.

rater1.notes: This is the same pattern as h022: Object.values(context) memoises on prop values. context is a new rest object every render, so [context] defeats the memo and re-renders all consumers each render.

Oxlint warns about .current in the cleanup, but context.hasSelectionRef and isPointerDownOnContentRef are stable flag refs, not DOM refs. The cleanup deliberately resets their current value to false on unmount. No fix is offered and none is needed.

rater2.notes: context.hasSelectionRef and context.isPointerDownOnContentRef hold boolean flags, not DOM nodes. Writing them in cleanup is an intended reset, not a stale read of a changed node. Oxlint only reports and no linter offers a fix.

rater1.notes: contentRef is a useRef object, which is stable, so removing it from the memo deps changes nothing.

rater2.notes: contentRef is a useRef object, so it is stable; dropping it from the shards memo's deps changes nothing.

rater1.notes: The dismiss listener never reads props.value, and a content instance keeps the same value, so dropping it only avoids a needless rebind. There is no comment saying whether it was meant as a trigger.

rater2.notes: The listener doesn't read props.value. Each viewport item is keyed by value, and each inline content belongs to one item, so value never changes for an instance. Listing or removing it makes no difference.

rater1.notes: _setVisible is an Effect Event (Radix's useEffectEvent) and by design is not a dependency. On React versions with native useEffectEvent the shim returns React's function, whose identity changes every render, so Biome's fix would re-add the form listeners on every render. With the fallback shim the function is stable. The worksheet's 'stable-value' sign only holds for the fallback.

rater2.notes: _setVisible comes from radix's useEffectEvent, which delegates to React's native useEffectEvent on 19.2+ (the repo uses 19.3). That returns a new function every render, so Biome's [inputRef, _setVisible] re-attaches the form reset/submit listeners on every render. The pre-19.2 shim is stable.

rater1.notes: ref is a useRef object, so [ref] and [] behave the same: the computed style is read once on mount.

rater2.notes: ref is a useRef object, so [ref] and [] behave the same: getComputedStyle is read once, on mount.

rater1.notes: This is the same as h028: ref is a stable useRef object, so removing it keeps the mount-only computed-style read.

The wheel handler only reads scrollbar, maxScrollPos and handleWheelScroll. viewport (context.viewport) is never read, so dropping it only avoids re-adding the document listener when the viewport element changes.

rater2.notes: The document wheel handler doesn't read viewport (context.viewport); it uses scrollbar and maxScrollPos. Removing viewport only skips a pointless re-subscription. It is likely a leftover.

rater1.notes: getItems is only used through getSortedTabbableCandidates, which already lists getItems in its own deps, so removing it here changes nothing.
The pause/resume handlers read the remaining time from refs, never duration. The separate open/duration effect resets the timer, so rebinding these listeners when duration changes has no effect.

handleRemoveGraceArea is not read here; its cleanup lives in the effect above. It changes only with onPointerInTransitChange, which handleCreateGraceArea already tracks, so removing it changes nothing.

rater2.notes: handleRemoveGraceArea isn't used in this effect. It and handleCreateGraceArea both depend only on onPointerInTransitChange, so they change together and dropping it changes nothing.

rater1.notes: dropState?.target is a deliberate invalidation key (see the comment): isDropTarget's answer only changes when the target changes. dropState and its isDropTarget method come from a state hook that returns a new object each render, so all three fixes would rebuild fn every render and re-render every drop indicator.

This is a dev warning checked once after mount (it needs the committed dragButtonRef). If dragState only appears after mount the warning is missed. dragState is a new state object each render, so adding it would repeat console.warn on every render; depending on !!dragState would be right.
sentinelRef is a useRef object, which is stable, so removing it from the memo deps changes nothing.

rater2.notes: sentinelRef is a useRef object, so it is stable; it can stay in the memoised object without being a dependency.

rater1.notes: onCloseEvent is an Effect Event, so leaving it out is by design. React Aria's useEffectEvent shim returns a stable callback, so adding it should be harmless; I couldn't read the shim in this sparse clone. If it were React's native useEffectEvent, the ref callback would rerun every render and re-scroll the sheet.

rater2.notes: onCloseEvent comes from react-aria's own useEffectEvent, which returns a stable useCallback(..., []) wrapper over a ref, so adding it to the ref callback's deps is a no-op.

rater1.notes: resizableDirection is a trigger: when it changes, the rendered data attributes (and so the CSS cursor) change, and the effect re-reads the computed cursor. Biome's fix drops it, so the cursor state would go stale.
tableRef is a useRef object, which is stable, so removing it from the context memo changes nothing (scrollRef is already left out for the same reason).
Every value the memo reads is listed, and no fix changes the array. The worksheet shows Biome's diagnostic with an empty message, so I can't tell what it flags.

This dev warning checks for an expand button once after mount. If hasChildItems flips to true later (children load), the missing-button warning is never shown. hasChildItems is a boolean, so [hasChildItems] re-checks only when it flips.

This is the same as h035: a mount-only dev warning that is missed if dragState appears later. dragState is a fresh state object each render, so [dragState] repeats the warning on every render; depending on !!dragState would be right.
elementRef is a useRef object, which is stable, so removing it from the mergeRefs memo changes nothing.
setOpenMobile is a useState setter, which is stable, so removing it from the context memo changes nothing.
setOpenMobile is a useState setter, which is stable, so removing it from toggleSidebar's deps changes nothing.

cancelChanges keeps the mount-time row, isEditable and onRowChange. row doesn't change while the editor is open (it never calls onRowChange(..., false)), but the grid's onRowChange is recreated per render and the stale one could carry old grid state. Adding the deps is safe because BlockKeys only re-reads onEscape when value changes.

The stale value is load-bearing: saveChanges compares the current value (passed in by BlockKeys) against the value captured at mount or when the full value loaded (isSuccess). Adding value makes the two always equal, so edits would close the popover without being committed. The baseline should be explicit (initial or loaded value in state or a ref).

This is the same as h046 in TextEditor: row stays fixed while editing (only committed onRowChange(..., true) calls), and a stale onRowChange from the grid is the only risk. The callback is only read by BlockKeys and onSelectExpand, so adding the deps is safe.
setFreeformText is a useState setter, which is stable, so removing it from the actions memo changes nothing.

requestDurationForm and databaseForm are react-hook-form useForm objects, which keep the same identity across renders, as do their reset methods, so adding them changes nothing. The effect copies fetched authConfig into the forms; RHF's values option or mounting the form once data has loaded would avoid it.

form (useForm) and its reset/setFocus methods are stable, so the effect still runs only when visible changes. Resetting the form when the dialog opens could live in the open handler, or come from remounting the dialog body.

With keepPreviousData, isSuccessCount stays true across filter changes, so forceExactCount isn't re-evaluated for new counts (a mild staleness). All three fixes write countData.count without ?., which throws while the first count query is pending. Even guarded, depending on countData would flip forceExactCount, part of the query key, back and forth.

The comment says this loads the localStorage filter and sort only once, when storage and count finish loading. Adding specificFilterColumn and sortByValue re-runs it whenever the URL value returns to the default 'email' or 'id:asc', which would override a URL or back-navigation choice with storage. The effective filter could instead be derived as url ?? storage.

isRevealedRef comes from useLatest, a ref object, which is stable, and the async callback deliberately reads .current after an await. Adding the ref (ESLint, Oxlint) changes nothing; Biome's isRevealedRef.current only rebuilds the callback when isRevealed changes, which is also harmless.

visible is a deliberate trigger to reset the form whenever the panel opens or closes; reset itself is stable. Biome's fix makes the reset mount-only, so values from a previous open would persist. Resetting in the open or close handler would remove the effect.

rater2.notes: visible is a trigger to reset the form when the panel opens or closes. Visibility is URL state (useQueryState), so Back can close the panel without closePanel's reset. Biome's [reset] resets only on mount. Keying the panel or resetting on open would replace the effect.

rater1.notes: isSuccessSchemas stands in for schemas, which arrive at the same moment. schemas keeps its reference between refetches (structural sharing) and setSelectedSchema is a nuqs setter, so the fixes behave the same. Biome's schemas?.find is Array.prototype.find. urlSchema is the same ?schema param the selector writes, so the effect barely does anything.

defaultValues is an object built during render, so adding it makes form.reset run on every render. Each reset updates form state and re-renders, which loops and wipes user edits. The comment says this initialises the form when data loads and preserves user changes afterwards, so the omission is deliberate.

The body never uses watchedTotalSize; the gp3 throughput limits are constants, so re-running on a size change does nothing. It looks left over (the comment mentions the 400 GB rule). Clamping throughput when storage type changes belongs in that field's change handler.
The worksheet classes emptyStateFallback as a constant, so it has fixed content and removing it from the memo deps changes nothing visible.

JSON.stringify(httpHeaders) deliberately compares headers by content, because useWatch hands back a cloned array (see the comment). Depending on httpHeaders by reference re-runs the effect and re-sets values.snippet on unrelated updates. Per its comment, the snippet should be rebuilt when the user changes a field, which is an event.

rater2.notes: httpHeaders comes from useWatch and gets a new array identity when its content hasn't changed. JSON.stringify(httpHeaders) tracks content, while every fix that adds httpHeaders re-runs the effect on identity changes and rewrites values.snippet, clobbering manual snippet edits, more often.

rater1.notes: The effect seeds the editable privileges state when the sheet opens and data has loaded. queuePrivileges is a .find() on query data, so ESLint's [queuePrivileges] is mostly harmless (stable under structural sharing). Oxlint's queuePrivileges.privileges and Biome's queuePrivileges.privileges.reduce throw at render whenever queuePrivileges is undefined (before load, or no match).

refreshKey is a deliberate trigger: as the comment says, it forces dayjs() to recompute the date range when the user clicks refresh. ESLint's and Biome's fixes drop it, so refresh would keep the old window; Oxlint leaves the array unchanged.

rater2.notes: refreshKey is the refresh button's trigger to recompute dayjs() 'now' (see the comment). Removing it means a refresh keeps the old start/end window.

rater1.notes: allAttributeKeys is rebuilt each render from an enum, so its content never changes. chartData is also rebuilt every render, so the memo already recomputes every render and adding allAttributeKeys changes nothing. The real fix is to hoist allAttributeKeys to module scope and memoise chartData.

refetchJsonSchema and refetchOpenAPISpec are React Query refetch functions, which are stable, so adding them keeps the effect firing only on rpcName changes. Refetching when the user opens a docs section is really a response to that navigation.

rater2.notes: refetchJsonSchema and refetchOpenAPISpec are TanStack Query refetch functions, bound once per observer and stable, so adding them changes nothing. The effect forces a refetch when the docs section (rpcName) changes, which the query layer or the nav handler could own.

rater1.notes: isSuccess flips in the same render that availableVersions goes from [] to the query array. That array keeps its identity because sort/reverse mutate it in place, so dropping isSuccess changes nothing. The effect re-asserts a valid form value, a workaround its comment explains.

runExplain is rebuilt whenever explainResults or explainLoadingQuery change. With it in the deps, a failed EXPLAIN resets the loading state, recreates runExplain and re-runs the effect, retrying EXPLAIN ANALYZE without end. ESLint's version also writes activeSheetRow.query without ?., which throws while no row is selected.

isPercentage is derived from chartData?.format, which is already listed, so nothing is stale; swapping format for isPercentage is equivalent. Oxlint's and Biome's fixes are harmless. ESLint's writes chartData.data without ?., which throws whenever chartData is undefined (loading, or another provider).
selectedDiffType and sourceSqlDiff are deliberate triggers for the syncDiffEditor Effect Event, which pushes the diff into the imperative Monaco diff editor. Biome's [] would sync only on mount.

diffRequest.pending and editorMountCount are deliberate triggers for the drainDiffRequest Effect Event (see the comment: the mount count re-runs it once the editor is ready). Biome's [] would drain only on mount and drop later AI diff requests.

Selection is seeded when the panel opens or addons load. If the subscription or project settings (hasHipaaAddon) arrive later, as on a deep link, the seed is stale. ESLint's [.., subscriptionPitr, hasHipaaAddon] is right (find() result and a boolean). Oxlint's and Biome's subscriptionPitr.variant.identifier throws whenever the project has no PITR addon.

defaultValues is rebuilt every render (draftFromRule or createDraft), so adding it calls form.reset on every render. The reset updates form state and re-renders, which loops and wipes user edits. The omission deliberately resets only when the sheet opens with data ready.

nodes and edges are deliberate triggers for the setReactFlow Effect Event, which reads both. Biome's fix drops edges, so an edge-only change would never re-run the dagre layout. The static reading event-specific does not fit.

The deps track lastColumn?.path and items.length instead of objects, because snap (a valtio snapshot) changes on every store update. In all three fixes lastColumn.items or hasMoreItems lose their ?., which throws while snap.columns is empty. Adding snap would also re-run the preview restore on unrelated store updates and could re-open a preview the user just closed.

rater2.notes: This is a URL-to-store preview sync that reacts only to chosen triggers (lastColumn?.path and items.length stand in for items). Adding snap (a valtio snapshot, new on every store write), lastColumn.items and setUrlPreview re-runs it on unrelated store updates. The stale case is items replaced at the same length, such as search results.

rater1.notes: lastItem (the last virtual row) is a deliberate trigger for the fetchNext Effect Event. Biome's [] would check only on mount, so infinite scroll would stop loading pages.

The form is seeded from the config only when the first load succeeds, so a later refetch with a different s3Protocol.enabled leaves the switch stale (rare). ESLint's and Biome's fixes are right: a boolean dep, and form is stable. Oxlint's config.features.s3Protocol.enabled has no ?., so it throws while config is loading.

rater2.notes: The form is reset only when the config query first succeeds, so a background refetch with a changed config.features.s3Protocol.enabled leaves the switch stale. form (useForm) is stable, so adding enabled syncs it without extra runs. RHF's values option could replace the effect.

rater1.notes: form (useForm) and form.reset are stable, so the effect still runs only when visible changes. Resetting on close could be done in onOpenChange or after submit, which already calls form.reset().

rater2.notes: form from useForm is a stable object, so [visible, form] behaves the same. The effect resets the form when visible (URL state) turns false, which a keyed sheet or the onOpenChange handler could do.

rater1.notes: onClose keeps the closePanel prop from the render where reset last changed. A parent closePanel that closes over changing state would be called stale, though most close handlers only set state. onClose goes to SidePanel's onCancel, so recreating it when closePanel changes is cheap.
This is the same as h077 in TextEditor: closePanel is captured stale. Adding it only recreates an onCancel handler, so the fix is safe.

rater2.notes: closePanel is either confirmOnClose (a stable useCallback over useLatest refs) or an inline arrow that only calls a state setter, so a stale copy behaves the same. Adding it only changes the identity of onClose, which is passed to SidePanel's onCancel.

rater1.notes: defaultPrivilegesQuery.status is a deliberate trigger for the syncDefaultPrivileges Effect Event. Biome's [] would never apply the default privileges once the query succeeds. Seeding editable state from query data could instead happen at initialisation.

setOpenRowId is a function rebuilt every render, so adding it runs the effect every render, re-setting ?id and firing track('unified_logs_row_clicked') again each time. Adding search.id also re-fires after the effect's own setSearch. The tracking and URL write belong in the row-select handler.

rater2.notes: setOpenRowId is a plain function declared in render, so adding it runs the effect on every render, firing track('unified_logs_row_clicked') and setSearch each time (and possibly looping through nuqs). search.id is only read as a condition. The URL write and the tracking belong in the row-select handler.

rater1.notes: pathname is a deliberate trigger to scroll the main container to the top on navigation. Biome's fix keeps only mainScrollContainer, so route changes would keep the old scroll position.

onFolderContentsChangeRef (useLatest) is a stable ref, so ESLint's and Oxlint's fix is harmless. Biome's .current tracks the parent callback, which SQLEditorNav passes inline and which calls setSubResults with a new object. The effect would then fire on every parent render and set parent state again, an infinite loop. The effect passes data up to the parent.

rater2.notes: onFolderContentsChangeRef comes from useLatest (a useRef updated during render), so ESLint's and Oxlint's fix that adds the ref is a no-op. Biome's onFolderContentsChangeRef.current would instead track the parent's inline handler, which sets parent state to a new object, and loop.

rater1.notes: The callback reads live data through useLatest refs and calls store methods that close over the valtio store, so nothing is stale. ESLint and Oxlint add tabs, a snapshot that changes on every store write. TableEditorMenu's effect depends on this callback, and removeRecentItems always assigns a new array, so the cleanup would re-run without end. Biome's version (prototype methods, tabsMap) only re-runs more.

createViewZone is a function rebuilt every render, so all three fixes remove and re-add the Monaco view zone and overlay widget on every render. Biome also drops beforeLineNumber and afterLineNumber, which createViewZone does read. Wrapping createViewZone in useCallback on [targetEditor, beforeLineNumber, afterLineNumber] would satisfy the rule correctly.

xAxisKey and yAxisKey are omitted but are constant for every caller, so this can't be seen today. stackedData is already memoised, so depending on it (or on stackedData[0], as Biome does) recomputes only when data changes. Stringifying the row is unnecessary.

variant is omitted, but the only caller passes the constant "percentages". ESLint's [dataKeys, stackedData, variant] and Oxlint's fix are right. Biome swaps JSON.stringify(stackedData) for stackedData.map and dataKeys.includes, which are Array.prototype methods and never change, so the percentages would stop updating when data changes.

table is the TanStack table instance from useDataTable context, which is stable, so adding it (or table.getAllColumns) changes nothing. The memo also sorts getAllColumns() in place, but that is unrelated.
columnId is a string prop that is constant per chart in practice. If it changed, the chart would keep the old key. Adding it is cheap and correct.

handlePaste only reads type and setTime, which are stable in practice, so its stale closure is harmless. startDate and endDate are not read and look left over. handlePaste is a function rebuilt every render, so adding it re-adds the document paste listener on every render; an Effect Event with [] fits.

rater2.notes: handlePaste is declared in render, so adding it re-subscribes the document paste listener on every render. It reads only type (constant per instance) and setTime (a state setter from the parent), so the stale copy is harmless; startDate/endDate are unused triggers.

rater1.notes: The effect syncs internal state from the from/to props only when the props change. Adding appliedStartDate and appliedEndDate re-runs it on every local apply or clamp and resets them to the props, undoing the clamp effect above. If from isn't in exact toISOString() form, the effect keeps re-setting a new Date, which loops.

queryClient from useQueryClient is stable, so adding it keeps the cleanup firing only when ref changes. The cleanup deliberately captures the departing ref, as the comment explains, to invalidate that project's React Query cache keys.

setActiveSnippet is a local useState setter, so removing it changes nothing. The effect applies a fetched snippet that the user asked to open (activeSnippetId in the store), then clears the request; that could be done in the handler that sets it.

rater2.notes: setActiveSnippet is a useState setter, so dropping it changes nothing. The effect loads a snippet once the user (or EditQueryButton) picks activeSnippetId and its query resolves, which could be done in that handler.

rater1.notes: setEditorPanelValue, setTemplates and setInitialPrompt are valtio store methods, and setSelectedIdToEdit is a nuqs setter, all stable across renders. Adding them doesn't change when the callback is rebuilt. (schema isn't read here, unlike the create handler above.)

id and chat?.name are deliberate triggers for the registerTab Effect Event: the page doesn't remount between chats, and a renamed chat updates its tab label. Biome's [] would register only the first chat.
id is a deliberate trigger for the registerTab Effect Event. The page component is reused across notebook ids, so Biome's [] would never add tabs for notebooks opened later.

This is a one-shot redirect once dashboard history loads, and history.sql and the tabs are read fresh at that moment. store is a valtio snapshot that changes on any tab update, and router changes per navigation, so adding them could fire router.replace repeatedly, possibly to a different target, before the redirect completes.

rater2.notes: The redirect deliberately runs once, when the dashboard history (local) finishes loading, and reads history.sql and the tabs store at that moment. Adding router (next/router, a new object across route changes) and the valtio store snapshot would re-fire router.replace on unrelated updates during the redirect.

rater1.notes: isSuccessOrganizations stands in for organizations. organizations defaults to a new [] while loading, so ESLint's and Oxlint's [organizations] run the effect every render until data arrives, and again whenever the list changes, overriding the selected slug. Biome's organizations[0]?.slug is right. The slug could be derived during render.

The mount-only async callback uses the first render's router. On a statically optimised page its query is still {} (the reason signInMethod goes through a useLatest ref), so the error redirects forward stale query params. But adding router (and router.query) re-runs auth.initialize() whenever the router changes, repeating redirects, addLoginEvent and the sign-in tracking. Reading the query through a ref or the Router singleton fixes it.

queryKey is a content hash of path and input and stands in for them. path (built by the proxy) and input are usually new each render, so ESLint's and Oxlint's fixes rebuild reset every render; the effect that calls reset then re-subscribes, updates state and re-renders without end. Biome's fix lists reset in its own deps, which throws a TDZ ReferenceError at render.

rater2.notes: queryKey is hashKey(path, input), a value-based stand-in for path (a fresh array from the decoration proxy on every call) and input (often inline). ESLint's [path, input] makes reset new every render, so the [reset] effect resubscribes in a loop. Biome's fix also lists reset in its own deps (TDZ error).

rater1.notes: hashKey(opts.queryKey) and opts.enabled cover what reset needs, and live callbacks go through optsRef. All three fixes add getInitialState and updateState, both consts declared below reset (lines 256 and 280), so the deps array throws a TDZ ReferenceError at render. Even reordered, ESLint's opts is a new object each render and would re-subscribe every render.

rater2.notes: getInitialState and updateState are declared after reset (and getInitialState depends on reset), so every linter's fix reads them before initialisation, a TDZ ReferenceError or TS2448 that breaks the hook. Even reordered, opts is a new object every render and would resubscribe constantly; hashKey(opts.queryKey) is the value-based key.

note: Rater 1 (a Claude subagent with read-only access to the clones) labelled every item; rater 2 (a separate Claude subagent, blind to rater 1) labelled the seeded subset in sample.json `blind`. Both raters are Claude models, so agreement measures how consistently the codebook applies, not independent human judgement. Shares are weighted to the flagged population by repo and stratum (sample.json strataPopulation).

values.mount-only: Run once (or only on some changes) on purpose
values.avoid-loop: Listing the dependency would loop or re-run too often
values.event-like: The omitted value is read like an event argument
values.stable-value: The omitted value is stable but the rule can't see it
values.workaround-now-wrong: A workaround that's no longer needed or now hides a real bug

fixWithoutSuppression.question: Is there a fix that needs no suppression?

values.ref: A ref for the latest value
values.memoise: Memoise a value or function (or move it out of the component)
values.add-dep-is-fine: Just add the dependency; nothing bad happens
values.none: No: the suppression is the best option

addingChangesBehaviour.question: Would adding the missing dependencies (the rule's suggestion) change behaviour?

justified.question: Is the suppression justified as written (would a careful reviewer keep it)?

rater1.notes: queryKey is a hash of path and input, standing in for them; input is usually an inline object, so listing it would recreate reset and resubscribe on every render. Reading input/path from a ref keyed on queryKey would avoid the comment.

opts is a fresh object each render, so listing it resubscribes every render; getInitialState and updateState are declared after reset, so adding them to its dependency array would also throw a TDZ ReferenceError. Reading opts from the existing optsRef plus a hoisted key variable would remove the need.

updateData is a new closure every ActionManager render, so the effect would re-run more often, but it is guarded by Object.keys(batchedData).length and batchedData is reset in the same commit, so the extra runs are no-ops (useEffectEvent would also express the intent).

Deliberate extra dependency used as a cache key: selectedFontFamily forces fonts.getSceneFamilies() to be re-read so hover previews don't change the list. ESLint's suggestion [fonts] drops it, and fonts is stable, so the set would never be recomputed; any rule-clean rewrite (state plus effect, or referencing the key in the body) is worse.

rater2.notes: selectedFontFamily is used as a cache key for a read of mutable scene state (app.fonts is a stable instance), so hover previews don't reshuffle the list; ESLint's suggestion [fonts] would never recompute. Only a state-plus-prop-change restructure avoids the comment, which is not clearly better.

rater1.notes: FontPicker passes onOpen/onClose as inline arrows, so listing them would run onClose (onPopupChange(false)) and onOpen after every parent render, closing and reopening the popup. Wrapping them in useEffectEvent keeps open/close tied to mount and unmount.

scrollPosition is a throttled atom updated while scrolling; as a dependency the effect would scroll back to a stale throttled offset during scrolling. Only the initial restore is wanted, which a useEffectEvent or an initial-value ref expresses.

Dynamic dependency list: the trails array itself is passed as deps so the effect re-runs only when a trail instance changes. App passes an inline array literal, so ESLint's [trails] would stop and restart every trail on each App render; storing the array once on the App instance would make [trails] safe.

rater2.notes: The trails array itself is passed as the dependency list so the effect compares the four trail instances element-wise; App passes a fresh inline array every render, so [trails] would stop and restart every trail on each App render. Making the array stable at the call site would remove the need.

rater1.notes: value, theme and placeholder are only initial config for the EditorView; theme and value have their own sync effects, so listing them would destroy and recreate the editor (losing history and cursor) on every keystroke. Only placeholder changes are silently ignored, a minor gap.
loadChats returns early when chatsLoaded or isLoading is set, so re-running the effect each time loadChats changes identity does nothing extra; the dependency could simply be listed.

The trigger set (message count, last id, isGenerating) is curated; saveCurrentChat changes with every chatHistory update, including currentPrompt edits, so listing it would persist chats on each prompt keystroke. useEffectEvent around the save keeps the curated trigger.

rater2.notes: The effect should fire on message count/generation completion, and saveCurrentChat (which changes with every chatHistory update, including the prompt) is called like an event handler; adding it would save on every chatHistory change once generation is idle. Wrapping the save in useEffectEvent keeps the trigger without the comment.

rater1.notes: Dead suppression: the controller memo only touches setDragState and refs (latestRef, stripRef), and neither linter reports anything with the comment removed. Delete the comment.

rater2.notes: The controller is meant to be created once, but everything it reads goes through latestRef/stripRef and the stable setDragState, so neither linter reports anything with the comment removed. The directive is dead and can simply be deleted.

rater1.notes: elementRef.current is listed on purpose so the observer is re-attached when the callback-ref element changes; ESLint's suggestion removes it, so a swapped element would stop being observed. Holding the element in state would be rule-clean but costs an extra render per Link, a plausible reason to keep it.

rater2.notes: The comment silences the unnecessary-dependency warning so elementRef.current can stay in the list to re-observe a new element, but deps are read at render before the callback ref writes, so it only catches the change on some later render. Holding the element in state via the callback ref would make re-observation deterministic without the hack.

rater1.notes: Variadic refs make the dependency list dynamic; the only rule-clean form (inline function with [refs]) gets a new array every render, so the composed ref would detach and reattach on every render. A ref-held stable callback would miss newly passed refs.

Dynamic dependency list from Object.values(context) memoises the provider value by its prop values; ESLint's [context] is a fresh rest object each render, so every consumer would re-render on each Provider render. A shallow-compare ref is the only alternative and is no clearer.
Same as the unscoped Provider: Object.values(context) keys the memo on prop values, while [context] is a new object every render and would defeat the memo for all consumers.
Oxlint-only false positive: the cleanup writes false to a flag ref from context (not a DOM ref that may have moved), which is the intended reset; ESLint does not flag it and there is nothing to add.
Same Oxlint-only cleanup-ref warning as the line above: resetting isPointerDownOnContentRef.current on cleanup is deliberate, and no dependency is missing.

rater2.notes: Oxlint-only warning about ref.current in cleanup, but these are context value refs holding booleans, not DOM nodes, and the cleanup deliberately writes false to the latest ref; ESLint says nothing. A false positive, so the suppression is the reasonable option.

rater1.notes: dropState is a new state object every render while isDropTarget only depends on the target, which is listed; adding dropState would recreate the render callback every render and invalidate drop-indicator rendering (perf only). A ref would make dropState?.target an unnecessary dependency that useCallback also flags.

rater2.notes: dropState is a fresh object from the stately hook every render, so listing it would give the render callback a new identity each render and re-render every item; keying on dropState.target is the intended invalidation. The callback runs during render, so a ref or useEffectEvent is off the table and memoising would mean changing the upstream hook.

rater1.notes: snap (a valtio snapshot) changes identity often, but the effect is guarded by isError, enforceExactCount and the 408 code, and after the first call enforceExactCount is false, so extra runs are no-ops.

rater2.notes: ESLint asks for the whole valtio snapshot only because snap.setEnforceExactCount is called as a method; the listed fields already cover the condition and the body is guarded and idempotent. Adding snap just re-runs a no-op more often.

rater1.notes: snap gets a new identity whenever the table state changes, including page itself, so listing it would reset to page 1 every time the user paginates. Calling setPage through useEffectEvent (or destructuring the stable setPage) keeps the trigger on filters only.

Listing router would re-run on every navigation, enforcing the MFA redirect away from any non-/org/[slug] page rather than only when the organization changes. Whether the MFA check should run on every navigation is a product decision the code doesn't settle.

defaultValues is rebuilt as a new object every render, so listing it would reset the notifications form on every render and wipe edits. Memoising it on authConfig (notificationsForm is the stable useForm object) makes the full list safe, a trivial local fix.

The spam check is meant to run when the template id changes; authConfig is refetched after every save (invalidateQueries), so listing it would re-run validateSpam after each save. The parent page only mounts the editor once the config has loaded, so the narrow trigger doesn't skip the first check.
form is the stable useForm object and isCreating is derived from hook, which only changes when definition or authConfig (already listed) change, so adding both causes no extra runs.

The forms are initialised once when the config query first succeeds; listing the config fields would re-reset both forms whenever server values change (for example after saving the rate-limit form, which would also discard unsaved edits in the IP-forwarding form). Saves already reset the form themselves.

rater2.notes: Initialises both forms once the auth config loads; listing every field would reset both forms whenever any field changes, so saving the IP-forwarding form would wipe unsaved rate-limit edits. useEffectEvent (or splitting into one effect per form) keeps the one-shot init without the comment.

rater1.notes: Unlike RateLimits, nothing resets the form after a successful save, and authConfig is refetched after the mutation, so with only [isSuccess, form] the form stays dirty (Cancel shown, Save enabled) after saving. Structural sharing means listing authConfig would only reset when the server data actually changes, which fixes that.

rater2.notes: Initialises the SMTP form when the config loads; react-query keeps authConfig's reference stable until the data actually changes, so adding it only re-syncs the form after a save invalidates the query. That is an improvement, since onSuccess here never resets the form and it stays dirty after saving.

rater1.notes: defaultValues is a constant object literal recreated every render, so listing it would reset the ban form on every render while visible. Hoisting it out of the component makes [visible, form, defaultValues] safe.

rater2.notes: Resets the ban form each time the modal opens; defaultValues is a fresh literal every render, so listing it would reset on every render (and every keystroke via useWatch). Hoisting the schema and constant defaults out of the component makes [visible, form] honest with identical behaviour.

rater1.notes: setFilters({...filters}) changes filters, so listing filters would re-run the effect after its own write (and its cleanup clears the f param), flapping or looping. An updater on the stable nuqs setter (setFiltersValue(prev => ...)) would remove the need to read filters.

rater2.notes: The effect writes the URL filters it reads, so listing filters would re-run after its own update (and the cleanup clears the param each time), risking a loop. Reading filters through useEffectEvent, or a functional update on the query state, keeps the run-on-user-change behaviour.

rater1.notes: forceExactCount is part of the count query key, so listing countData would flip-flop: an exact result has is_estimate false, which sets it back to false, which refetches the estimate. Only ever setting it to true would be rule-clean; as written the decision is made once per success and isn't revisited when filters change, which may or may not be intended.

updateSortByValue, onSelectImpersonateUser and onSelectViewLogs are new functions every render and the effect calls setColumns, so the full list would loop. The columns are derived data (useMemo plus memoised handlers would avoid the effect), and the captured handlers can go stale (updateSortByValue reads isCountWithinThresholdForSortBy), so it's hard to say the omission is harmless.

The comment says load the localStorage filter and sort once; listing specificFilterColumn and sortByValue would re-run on every user change and push the stored values back (selecting 'email' or 'id:asc' would be undone). useEffectEvent or a done-once ref expresses the intent.

form is stable, selectedSchema can't change while the sheet is open, and the func fields are primitives from query data that only change if the function is edited elsewhere while the sheet is open (saving closes the sheet). Listing them changes nothing in normal use.

rater2.notes: Initialises the function form when the sheet opens or a different function is chosen; listing every func field and selectedSchema would also reset in-progress edits whenever a refetch or the page's schema selector changes them. useEffectEvent keeps the one-shot reset without the comment.

rater1.notes: tables is rebuilt (sort().filter()) every render, so listing it would reset the trigger form on every render while open, wiping edits. Reading tables and the trigger through useEffectEvent keeps reset tied to open and data readiness.

defaultValues is a new object literal every render, so listing it would call form.reset on every render once data has loaded, discarding the user's disk changes. The reset should only fire when the load flags change.

useWatch returns a new httpHeaders array even when the content is unchanged, so the JSON.stringify key stands in for it; listing httpHeaders would regenerate and overwrite the snippet on every render. A deep-equality memo of httpHeaders (or deriving the snippet at submit) would be rule-clean.

Second comment on the same hook, covering the complex-expression warning for JSON.stringify(httpHeaders); same reasoning: the stringified key avoids re-running on every new headers array, and a deep-equal memo would remove both comments.

rater2.notes: useWatch returns a new httpHeaders array each render, so depending on it re-runs the effect (which calls setValue) on every render; the comment explains the JSON.stringify key. Hoisting the stringified headers into a variable and parsing it inside the effect would give an honest, stable dependency.

rater1.notes: defaultValues is rebuilt every render, so listing it would reset the cron form on every render while open. pgCronExtension comes from cached query data, so reading it through useEffectEvent keeps reset tied to opening.

rater2.notes: Resets the cron form when the sheet opens; defaultValues is rebuilt every render (it includes parsed command values), so listing it would reset on every render and wipe typing. useEffectEvent, or memoising defaultValues, removes the need for the comment.

rater1.notes: generateCronSyntax is TanStack Query's mutate, which is stable (useCallback over the observer), so listing it adds no runs.

rater2.notes: generateCronSyntax is TanStack Query v5's mutate, which is a stable useCallback over the observer, so the rule just can't see it is stable. Adding it changes nothing.

rater1.notes: Deliberate extra dependency: refreshKey forces calculateDateRange to recompute relative to now so a refresh moves the window; ESLint's [interval] would freeze the dates until the interval changes. Computing without the memo would change the query keys every render, so the suppression is the clearest option.

buildSlowQueriesCountSql() returns a constant string, so recomputing it on refreshKey yields an identical SQL and query key and never forces a refetch. The suppressed refresh trigger does nothing; ESLint's [] behaves the same.
form is the stable useForm object and both listed values are memoised, so adding form changes nothing.

Listing router.query.source and subscription?.plan?.name would re-run when the subscription loads or the source changes, resetting the panel state and sending a second opened event. The component already has the onPanelOpened effect event; reading those two values inside it would make [visible] rule-clean.
Dead suppression: the reason (v5 not recognising useEffectEvent) no longer applies, and neither linter reports anything with the comment removed. Delete it.
The effect only writes when form.getValues('role') is empty, so re-running it when orgScopedRoles changes identity is a no-op; form is stable.

rater2.notes: Sets the default Developer role when the sheet opens; form is stable and orgScopedRoles is the query's array, and the body only acts while the role is still empty, so extra runs are no-ops. Listing both is harmless.

rater1.notes: member is parent state set when the panel opens and allRoles is query data, so neither changes while the panel is open; listing them adds no realistic runs.

rater2.notes: Seeds the panel's local role configuration from the member and roles each time it opens; listing member and allRoles would re-seed and discard unsaved edits whenever the roles query refetches with changed data. useEffectEvent keeps the open-time seed without the comment.

rater1.notes: Extra dependency with no role: startDate is computed purely from dateRange, so dropping subscription (ESLint's [dateRange]) gives the same strings at the same times.

Extra dependency: endDate reads dayjs() but subscription only changes identity when its data changes (structural sharing), so it is not a meaningful refresh trigger; [dateRange] behaves the same in practice.

Documented choice: allSelectableRegions is a new array every render, so listing it runs the effect every render; the effect is idempotent, so the visible result is the same, it just runs constantly. Reading the list through useEffectEvent keeps the trigger on dbRegion without the comment.

runExplain changes whenever explainResults or explainLoadingQuery change; on an error neither result is stored, so listing it would re-run the effect and retry EXPLAIN in a loop. useEffectEvent keeps it triggered only by the sheet view and query.

Subscribe-once route listener: router.events is stable, and re-subscribing when asPath or an inline onCurrentSelectQuery changes would churn listeners without changing what the handler does. useEffectEvent for the handler is the textbook fix.

One-way sync from local search to the URL; listing urlSearch would also run when the URL changes, writing the local value back over external changes (including the route-change handler's search: null).

state is a valtio snapshot whose identity changes after store mutations, so listing it would re-run setSelectedDatabaseId(ref) after the user picks a read replica and reset them to primary. Calling the stable method through useEffectEvent (or destructuring it) keeps the trigger on ref.

onSearchQueryChange is redefined every render, so listing it would write the debounced value to the URL on every render, overwriting any other change to search. Calling setSearchParams directly in the effect or via useEffectEvent removes the need.

This component reads state.selectedDatabaseId, so the snapshot changes whenever a replica is selected; listing state would immediately reset the selection to the primary. Only ref changes should trigger it.

config and onChangeConfig must stay out (onChangeConfig({...config, token}) changes config, which would refetch a temporary key in a loop), but jwtSecret is also omitted: if the PostgREST config loads after the keys, the bearer is never recomputed until the role changes. useEffectEvent for the config update, with jwtSecret listed, would fix both.

rater2.notes: The effect writes config through onChangeConfig, so listing config would refetch a token and update config forever. onChangeConfig is a setState dispatcher, so a functional update (prev => ({ ...prev, token, bearer })) removes config from the deps, and jwtSecret/projectRef can then be listed, which also stops jwtSecret going stale.

rater1.notes: snapV2 changes on every editor store update, so listing it would re-register the formatter constantly; but the provider closes over the first id, and the SQL editor isn't remounted per snippet, so formatting can write to the wrong snippet. Reading id and the store from a shared ref (as done for sharedPgInfoRef) avoids both.

rater2.notes: Registers the shared format provider once per monaco/enabled to avoid re-registering on every snapshot change, but the provider closes over the first id, and the SQL editor provider is not keyed per snippet, so formatting after switching snippets can write to the old snippet. Reading id and setSql through useEffectEvent or a latest ref fixes that without re-registering.

rater1.notes: resetFormRef comes from useLatest, a ref object that is stable for the component's lifetime; the rule just can't see that through the custom hook.
defaultValues is rebuilt every render (draftFromRule/createDraft), so listing it would reset the rule form on every render while open. The reset is meant to fire on opening once data is ready.

Listing selectedOrg would re-run while open and immediately clear the user's selection via setSelectedOrg(undefined). The reset and the cache removal belong in the open and close handlers, which needs no effect.
setPollIntervalNamespaceTables is a useState setter passed down from the parent, so it is stable and adding it changes nothing.

The join(',') key lets callers pass a fresh array without recreating the picker store; listing acceptedFileExtensions would rebuild the store (losing selection) whenever the array identity changes. Memoising or hoisting the array at call sites would make it safe.

snap changes on every store update; with it listed, the effect would re-run after a file is opened but before the URL catches up (urlPreview still null) and clear the preview. The file already uses useEffectEvent, which could read items, hasMoreItems, snap and setUrlPreview here.

form is stable and config?.features.s3Protocol.enabled is a primitive that only changes when the server value changes (after a save it equals the value already reset in onSuccess), so listing it changes nothing in practice.
generateAttachmentURLs is TanStack Query's mutateAsync, which is bound once per observer and stable, so listing it (and narrowing profile to its two fields as ESLint suggests) changes nothing.

form is stable, conversationId is a fixed prop for the form's lifetime, and organizations is query data that keeps its identity unless the list actually changes, so listing them adds no realistic runs.

foreignKeys is rebuilt with filter() every render, so listing it would re-run and call setColumnFields every render, looping. But foreignKeyMeta is also frozen at open time: TableEditor needed a separate re-init effect for FK metadata that arrives after the panel opens, and ColumnEditor has none, so this may hide the same late-data bug.
foreignKey comes from parent useState (selectedFk) that is set before opening and doesn't change while the selector is open, so listing it adds no runs.

validateType is redefined every render and calls setErrors with a new object, so listing it would loop. It also reads selectedTable, which loads asynchronously, and the effect doesn't re-validate when it arrives; deriving the type errors during render would fix both.

onUpdateField is redefined every render, so listing it would re-apply the imported columns on every render, overwriting later edits. The import is a one-off event; useEffectEvent (or applying it in the import callback) removes the need.
setSearch comes from nuqs useQueryStates with a module-level parser map, so it is stable and listing it changes nothing.

setOpenRowId is redefined every render and search.id changes after the effect's own setSearch, so the full list would re-run the effect and fire the unified_logs_row_clicked event repeatedly. track and the setters belong in an effect event.

storedFeedback is rewritten by the debounced persist effect below, so listing it would re-run the hydration after each save and could overwrite keystrokes typed since the debounce snapshot. The comment's stated intent (hydrate once) is right.
As the comment says, setStoredFeedback is stable (useLocalStorageQuery's useCallback over the key and queryClient), which is exactly why listing it would cost nothing; the suppression is unnecessary.

rater2.notes: The stated reason is right: useLocalStorageQuery's setter is a useCallback over a constant key and the query client, so it is stable. That is exactly why listing it costs nothing and the comment is unnecessary.

rater1.notes: Listing project would re-run when the project loads; with no sidebar open yet that clears the sidebar URL param and localStorage before the restore effect reads them, and with one open it re-sends the sidebar_opened event. The body could move into an effect event alongside onSidebarChanged.
openSidebar is a function from the valtio store (same reference in every snapshot) and sidebarLocalStorageRef is a useLatest ref, so both are stable and listing them changes nothing.

In this codebase formatDocument is either the module-level default or an inline disabled object, so listing it changes nothing; as a shared component the omission also leaves formatDocument.callback stale. A callback ref like the file's runQueryCallbackRef would be the robust fix.

rater2.notes: formatDocument.callback is invoked later by the provider like an event handler. In this codebase formatDocument is either the module-level DEFAULT_ACTIONS object (stable) or an inline object with enabled false (no-op), so listing it changes nothing; a latest ref or useEffectEvent (as the file already does for runQuery) would be the robust option for future inline callers.

rater1.notes: Copy of Radix's useComposedRefs: the dependency list is the variadic refs, and the only rule-clean form ([refs] with an inline function) changes every render, detaching and reattaching the ref each time.

state is a valtio snapshot and this component reads selectedDatabaseId, so the snapshot changes whenever the user picks a database; listing it would push the prop value back into the store and override the choice. Only prop changes should sync.

The applied dates are read only to skip redundant updates; listing them would re-run after every internal apply and reset the applied range to the props before the parent catches up (or loop if the parent's string format differs from toISOString()). Adjusting state on prop change during render, or making it controlled, avoids the effect.

rater2.notes: Syncs internal applied dates from the to/from props only when the props change; the applied state is read for comparison. Listing it would re-run right after an internal apply and revert it to the old prop until (or unless) the parent echoes the new value, so reading it via useEffectEvent is the clean alternative.

rater1.notes: queryClient from useQueryClient is the stable context client, so [queryClient] still runs the cleanup only on unmount.
queryClient is stable, so adding it keeps the cleanup tied to ref changes exactly as now.

rater2.notes: The only missing dependency is the QueryClient from useQueryClient, which is stable for the provider's lifetime. Listing it keeps the per-ref cleanup exactly as it is.

rater1.notes: Listing selectedFileId would rebuild the tree (resetting every node's isEditing) whenever the selection changes, cancelling an in-progress rename. Splitting the select-first-file logic into its own effect, or deriving the tree with useMemo, needs no suppression.
onInitialLoad is a callback prop (often inline) and projects falls back to a new []; listing them would call onInitialLoad on every render instead of once when the first load completes.

snap changes identity after store mutations; listing it would re-run when the panel is closed (setPanelKey(undefined)) while the panel query param is still in the URL, reopening the panel and re-scrolling.

router changes identity on hydration and navigation; the same codebase documents (TableEditorPage) that re-firing a redirect effect on router changes pushed the same URL repeatedly and froze the page. lastVisitedOrganization itself is stable once loaded.

rater2.notes: A one-shot redirect once the last-visited org resolves; lastVisitedOrganization is a stable string once isSuccess is true and router is only used for push. A new router object could at most repeat a push to the same URL, which is harmless.

rater1.notes: useFlag returns false both before flags load and when the flag is off, so on a hard load the value never changes when hasLoaded flips and the redirect never fires, leaving a blank page (the component renders null). Listing hasLoaded fixes this with no downside.
templateForm is the stable useForm object, so listing it changes nothing.

Documented in the comment: useRouter() returns a new object on navigation renders, and listing router re-fired the redirect mid-navigation and froze the page; the tab store snapshot and history would add more re-runs. useEffectEvent for the redirect is the clean fix.
form is the stable useForm object; the state setters are already exempt, so listing form changes nothing.

router changes identity on navigation renders; as TableEditorPage documents in the same codebase, listing it re-fires the redirect mid-navigation. Reading router from an effect event keeps the trigger on the flags.

rater2.notes: Only router is omitted, presumably because the pages-router object changes identity on navigation; the effect is condition-guarded and only calls router.replace to a fixed URL, so an extra run is at worst a redundant replace.

rater1.notes: snapV2 is the SQL editor store snapshot and changes on every edit; listing it would call setSnippet(ref, data) with the fetched server copy after each keystroke, clobbering local edits. Only new data, project or ref should trigger it.
The redirect to the last snippet is meant for landing on /new; listing router (new identity on navigation renders) and history.sql would re-fire it mid-navigation or whenever history updates.

rater2.notes: Redirects from /new to the last visited snippet; it already re-runs on every allSnippets change, so listing skip, history.sql, router and ref adds little risk, and it would also catch dashboard history (an async localStorage query) resolving after the snippets. Guards keep extra runs to at most a redundant replace.

rater1.notes: tabs is a valtio snapshot that changes on every tab change; listing it would re-add the current tab right after the user closes it. The next effect in the file already uses useEffectEvent for exactly this reason.
Dead suppression: its reason (old plugin not ignoring useEffectEvent) no longer holds, and neither linter reports anything with it removed.

rater2.notes: The reason cites eslint-plugin-react-hooks v5 mishandling useEffectEvent, but the repo locks v7.1.1 and neither ESLint nor Oxlint reports anything with the comment removed. The directive is stale and can be deleted.

rater1.notes: The effect's own removeTab/removeSnippet calls change the tabs and snapV2 snapshots while isSnippetDeleted stays true, so listing them would re-run it and repeat the toast and router.replace.

One-shot redirect once history loads; listing router and the tab store snapshot would re-fire router.replace on navigation renders and tab changes, the same failure documented for the table editor index.

Listing router (new identity on navigation renders) would re-fire the toast and push while navigating away. Deleting the current bucket navigates explicitly, so the narrow isSuccess trigger doesn't strand the user.
Same pattern as the analytics bucket page: router would re-fire the not-found toast and push during navigation; bucket deletion already navigates away itself.
Same pattern as the other bucket pages: listing router re-fires the toast and push mid-navigation; the one-shot check on isSuccess is the intent.

rater2.notes: Redirects when the bucket isn't found once the query succeeds; listing bucket and bucketId would also re-check on client navigation to another bucket or when a refetch drops it, which is the correct behaviour, and router/ref are only used to build the push.

rater1.notes: organizations only changes identity while loading (the [] default, when the effect does nothing new) or when the list really changes; setSlug bails out on equal values, so listing it adds no visible runs.

Auth initialisation must run once; router changes identity when isReady flips after hydration, so listing it could run initialize() again and send a duplicate login event and redirect. addLoginEvent and queryClient are stable.

rater2.notes: Initialising auth once is right, and listing the pages-router object would re-run the whole flow (duplicate tracking and login events) on router changes. But the async callbacks read router.query from the mount-time router snapshot, which can be empty before isReady; moving the post-initialize handling into useEffectEvent (or a latest ref, as done for signInMethod) avoids that.
